newsitem.title: UK: BT head urges shareholders to approve merger.
newsitem.headline: BT head urges shareholders to approve merger.

text.p: The chairman of British Telecommunications plc on Tuesday urged shareholders to approve the company's proposed $20 billion merger with U.S. telecoms carrier MCI Communications Corp since it was the key to unlocking long term shareholder value.
BT Chairman Sir Iain Vallance told shareholders at an extraordinary general meeting if BT is "to develop and grow, it will do so most successfully with MCI" in its Concert Plc joint venture.
"We have the chance to make Concert one of the great companies of the late 20th century, and to create one of the first great companies of the 21st century," he said.
He said the proposed marriage "will be the world's best market defender coupled with the world's best market attacker."
Vallance said that the global telecommunications market is already huge - more than $650 billion today, and expected to top a trillion dollars by the year 2000.

At the moment BT and MCI have a six per cent share of that global market, but outside the United States and the UK only 17 percent of the market is open to competition; by the year 2000 that could be 95 percent, he said.
"There is a great opportunity here. Were we to do nothing more than to hold on to that six per cent, Concert would have revenues of 34 billion stg within a few years," Vallance said.
Vallance said Concert would primarily focus on Europe and the U.S. but within a "few years" be as active in Asia and Latin America.
